title: Catalan Opening: the ideas
line: The Queen's Gambit with a bishop on the long diagonal, aimed at Black's queen's side.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, into the center.

also.e2e4: That is the king's pawn opening, the other big first move. This lesson goes on with the queen's pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c2 two squares. It attacks the center from the side and takes space.

also.g1f3: Bringing the knight out first is also sound and often comes to the same thing. This lesson goes on with the pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on g2 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.b1c3: That allows the Nimzo-Indian Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn.
also.g1f3: That leads to the Queen's Indian or the Bogo-Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn.

steps.after: This is the Catalan Opening. Black holds the center with a pawn.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. It looks through the center at Black's queen's side.
Bring the knight out, ready to castle.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
Tap every black piece and pawn on your bishop's long diagonal.
steps.hint: Follow the diagonal from the bishop toward the far corner.
steps.after: When the center opens, the bishop hits Black's queen's side: the pawn there and the rook in the corner.

steps.text: Bring the queen out. It guards the pawn on c4 and gets ready to help a pawn to e4.

summary: White's bishop on the long diagonal looks through Black's center at the queen's side, waiting for the center to open.
